people.name: Adam Schlesinger
people.description: American singer-songwriter, record producer and guitarist Adam Schlesinger, best known for his work with Fountains Of Wayne and for its 2003 Grammy-nominated single 'Stacy's Mom'. Schlesinger died on 1 April 2020 from complications brought on by COVID-19.

people.name: Adam Horovitz
people.description: American rapper, guitarist, and actor Ad-Rock, (Adam Horovitz), from The Beastie Boys, the American hip-hop group that formed in New York City in 1981. They scored the 1987 US No.7 & UK No.11 single 'You Gotta Fight For Your Right To Party', and the 1987 US No.1 and UK No.7 album Licence To Ill, (the first rap album to top the Billboard 200 chart). The Beastie Boys have sold 20 million records in the United States and had seven platinum-selling albums from 1986 to 2004. They are the biggest-selling rap group since Billboard began recording sales in 1991.

people.name: Annabella Lwin
people.description: English-Burmese singer, songwriter Annabella Lwin, best known as the singer with Bow Wow Wow, who scored the 1982 UK No.7 single 'Go Wild In The Country'. Bow Wow Wow signed a recording contract with EMI Records in July 1980, and released their first single, 'C·30 C·60 C·90 Go!', shortly afterwards. Originally only released on cassette, it was the world's first-ever cassette single.

people.name: Colm O\'Ciosoig
people.description: Irish musician and songwriter Colm O'Ciosoig, from the Irish-English rock band My Bloody Valentine. They scored the 1991 UK No.29 single 'To Here Knows When'. Signed to Creation Records in 1988, they are widely cited as a pioneering act in the shoegaze genre. He has also worked with Hope Sandoval & the Warm Inventions and toured with Sandoval's band Mazzy Star.

people.name: Mikkey Dee
people.description: Swedish rock musician and multi-instrumentalist Mikkey Dee, best known as the last drummer for British rock band Motorhead from 1991 until its dissolution following the death of Lemmy in December 2015.

people.name: Johnny Marr
people.description: British-born Irish musician, singer and songwriter Johnny Marr. He was the guitarist and songwriter with English rock band The Smiths who had the 1984 UK No.10 single 'Heaven Knows I'm Miserable Now', plus 15 other UK Top 40 singles. With Electronic, he had the 1991 UK No.8 single 'Get The Message' and with Modest Mouse, the 2007 US No.1 album ‘We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank’. Marr has also worked with The The, The Pretenders, The Cribbs, and Johnny Marr and the Healers. As a prolific session musician, Marr has worked with names such as Kirsty MacColl, Pet Shop Boys, Talking Heads, Bryan Ferry, and Hans Zimmer. On 19 July 2012, Marr received an honorary doctorate from the University of Salford for "outstanding achievements" and "changing the face of British guitar music".

people.name: Larry Mullen
people.description: Larry Mullen Jr. Irish musician best known as the drummer of U2. Their 1987 UK and worldwide No.1 album Joshua Tree spent 156 weeks on the UK chart. U2 scored five consecutive US No.1 albums from 1987. U2 are one of the world's best-selling music artists, having sold an estimated 150–170 million records worldwide. Their accolades include 22 Grammy Awards, eight Brit Awards, four Ivor Novello Awards, and two Golden Globe Awards. According to Pollstar, they were the second-highest-grossing live music artist from 1980 to 2022, earning US$2.13 billion.

people.name: Tony Bowers
people.description: Tony Bowers, from Alberto Y Los Trios Paranoias and then Simply Red, who had the 1986 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Holding Back The Years'.

people.name: Bernard Edwards
people.description: American bassist and record producer Bernard Edwards. As a member of Chic, Edwards created era-defining hits such as 'Dance, Dance, Dance', 'Everybody Dance', 'Le Freak', 'I Want Your Love' and 'Good Times'. Edwards also worked with Nile Rodgers to produce and write for other artists, using Chic to perform everything musically and vocally except lead vocals, working with Sister Sledge, Sheila and B. Devotion, Diana Ross, Johnny Mathis, Debbie Harry. He produced records for ABC, Power Station and Rod Stewart. Just before a concert at the Budokan Arena in Tokyo on April 18, 1996, Edwards fell ill, but refused to cancel the gig. After the show, Edwards retired to his hotel room, where he was later found dead by Nile Rodgers.

people.name: Moon Martin
people.description: American singer, songwriter and guitarist Moon Martin. Originally a rockabilly artist, he wrote the songs ‘Bad Case of Loving You (Doctor, Doctor)’, made famous by the English singer Robert Palmer, and ‘Cadillac Walk’, a hit for American singer Willy DeVille. Hi died on 11 May 2020 age 74.

people.name: Russ Ballard

Ballard has written songs for many artists including, Roger Daltrey, America, Three Dog Night, Santana and Brian May.

people.name: Jaap Eggermont
people.description: Dutch record producer, Jaap Eggermont best known for his Stars on 45 project and as the drummer of the band Golden Earring. Stars on 45 recorded hit songs as faithfully as possible as a medley and joined them together with a common tempo and underlying drum track.

people.name: Tom Paxton
people.description: American folk singer-songwriter Tom Paxton. His songs have been recorded by many artists including: Bob Dylan, Sandy Denny, Joan Baez, The Seekers, Marianne Faithfull, John Denver, Dolly Parton and Porter Wagoner, Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson and The Move. In 2009, Paxton received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.

works.title: The Boy Who Played the Harp
works.eventDescription: Dave became the first British rap artist to debut three albums at No.1 on the UK's official chart. His latest, The Boy Who Played The Harp, knocked Taylor Swift's Life of a Showgirl off the top spot, and managed to fend off competition from Lily Allen's much talked-about West End Girl. According to the Official UK Charts Company, it also became the fastest-selling rap album on vinyl this century. His previous two albums also re-entered the top 40, making him the first British rap act to have three entries in the chart simultaneously.

works.title: Hackney Diamonds

The album went to No.1 in 20 countries and was promoted with an extensive, worldwide advertising campaign. On 17 August 2023, an advertisement appeared in the Hackney Gazette teasing the album, referencing several Rolling Stones song titles and displaying their tongue logo.

works.title: Blurred Lines
works.eventDescription: Marvin Gaye's family were taking legal action against Robin Thicke and Pharrell Williams for copyright infringement over their hit song Blurred Lines. Three of Gaye's children filed legal papers accusing them of copying elements of the song 'Got To Give It Up'. The Gaye family cited excerpts of magazine interviews given by Thicke to support their claim he had admitted to drawing on 'Got to Give it Up' when producing Blurred Lines.

works.title: Abbey Road
works.eventDescription: The white suit worn by John Lennon on the cover of the Beatles' Abbey Road album sold for $118,000 (£66,385) at an auction in Las Vegas. And an Austin Princess hearse driven by the late star in the documentary Imagine sold for $150,000 (£84,388). A portion of the proceeds from the sale of the items went to Amnesty International.

works.title: Believe
works.eventDescription: Chart history was made when the UK Top 5 singles chart was made up entirely of new entries. Alanis Morissette went in at No.5, Culture Club at No.4, U2 at No.3, George Michael at No.2 and Cher with 'Believe' at No.1. It made Cher (who was 52) the first female artist to have a No.1 single over the age of 50. The song was a No.1 in 23 countries.

works.title: End of the Road

works.title: Give Peace a Chance
works.eventDescription: UK DJ Roger Scott died of cancer aged 46. Scott was one of the most respected broadcasters in the UK, working on Capital Radio for 15 years and then BBC Radio 1. Working as a presenter at the Montreal station 1470 CFOX, Scott sang on ‘Give Peace a Chance’, recorded by John Lennon and Yoko Ono during their "Bed-in" for peace at the Queen Elizabeth Hotel in Montreal, Canada.

works.title: Silk Torpedo
works.eventDescription: Led Zeppelin held the UK launch for their new record label Swan Song at Chislehurst Caves, Kent, England on Halloween night. Drinks were served by nuns in suspenders, a naked woman lay in a coffin covered in jelly and naked male wrestlers cavorted in recesses of the caves. Label mates Bad Company, The Pretty Things and Maggie Bell also attended. The launch also tied in with the releases of The Pretty Things new album Silk Torpedo. The label was named after an unreleased Zeppelin instrumental track.

works.title: Led Zeppelin III

works.title: Space Oddity
works.eventDescription: David Bowie appeared at a Halloween night at the General Gordon, Gravesend, England. The gig lasted about 15 minutes, after Bowie sang 'Space Oddity' to everyone’s delight and then dragged a stool on stage, along with a huge book. He then sat and read poems and was booed off stage.

works.title: Bad Case of Loving You (Doctor, Doctor)
works.eventDescription: American singer, songwriter and guitarist Moon Martin. Originally a rockabilly artist, he wrote the songs ‘Bad Case of Loving You (Doctor, Doctor)’, made famous by the English singer Robert Palmer, and ‘Cadillac Walk’, a hit for American singer Willy DeVille. Hi died on 11 May 2020 age 74.

works.title: Hold Your Head Up
works.eventDescription: Singer, songwriter and musician Russ Ballard from English rock band Argent who had the 1972 UK No.5 single 'Hold Your Head Up' and the hit and 'God Gave Rock and Roll to You'. Ballard has written songs for many artists including, Roger Daltrey, America, Three Dog Night, Santana and Brian May.
